events.title: Certiorari granted and case remanded in Williams v. Charleston County Sheriff
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Williams, Randall, et al. v. Charleston County Sheriff, et al. The judgment was vacated, and the case was remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit for further consideration in light of a recent decision in Galette v. New Jersey Transit Corp. This procedural action indicates that the Fourth Circuit must reevaluate the case with the new precedent in mind.
events.why_relevant: The remand for reconsideration in light of new precedent affects the legal landscape and the application of law in similar cases.

events.title: Supreme Court reverses Second Circuit decision in Zorn v. Linton
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari and reversed the Second Circuit's decision in the case of Jacob P. Zorn v. Shela M. Linton. The case involved a protester, Shela Linton, who claimed excessive force was used by Sergeant Jacob Zorn during her arrest at a sit-in protest. The Second Circuit had previously ruled that Zorn was not entitled to qualified immunity, but the Supreme Court found that the Second Circuit failed to identify a case where similar actions were held to violate the Constitution. The Court concluded that Zorn was entitled to qualified immunity.
events.why_relevant: This decision clarifies the application of qualified immunity in cases involving claims of excessive force by law enforcement.

events.title: Supreme Court releases opinion in Zorn v. Linton (25-297)
events.summary: The Supreme Court released an official slip opinion in Zorn v. Linton. Docket number(s): 25-297.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's official opinion in Zorn v. Linton is a primary legal source. Supreme Court opinions can define binding national law and alter the legal position of the executive branch, federal agencies, states, litigants, and democratic institutions.
